raw_comment:
The first thing I notice when looking at the graph is how almost every single part of the country has some sort of drought going on. While there are areas that remain uncolored, which I am assuming there is no drought occurring in those places, most are the very least abnormally dry. I also notice that there are very certain sections that have an extreme or exceptional drought happening that are scattered in different areas of the country, it is not in one particular area. 
I wonder how this graph would compare to a graph of last year's droughts. I also wonder if the areas experiencing droughts are also facing high rates of forest fires as well. Finally, I wonder if this has a large impact on farming.
This relates to my community because in NJ, where I reside, there was a large period of time we went without water and in a drought. While we have gotten snow and rain in the recent months, NJ remains in drought warning. Not only this, but these droughts are a direct result of climate change which effects every individual in the world. 
Headline: The United States of Droughts
